blocks.content: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every second year.

rows: Speaker (Elected by members of Lok Sabha)
Limited power (Can delay up to 14 days)
Exclusive power to introduce and pass Money Bills

items: Article 249: Rajya Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest.
Article 312: Special power to create one or more new All-India Services by passing a resolution with a two-thirds majority.
Money Bills: Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only withhold it for a maximum period of 14 days.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of Indian Parliament, representing the States and Union Territories.
It is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.
The Vice-President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Twelve members are nominated by the President from fields of Art, Literature, Science, and Social Service.
